correctness.rationale: For any m>=3 and equal radius r>0 disks centered (with repetition allowed) on the radius-R circle, partial probe-circle coverage equals Σ_j min(g_j,2 alpha(rho)), where alpha(rho)=arccos((R²+rho²-r²)/(2Rrho)) and Σg_j=2pi. This immediately proves equal-gap regular centers maximize every nonnegative radial integral. Equality is all pairwise disjoint centers for r<R sin(pi/m), and uniquely regular centers at and above that threshold because a strict gap inequality appears on positive-measure radii. Exact radial-ray integration reproduces three area branches for 0<r<=Rs, Rs<r<R and r>=R. At first tangency, two-disk lens asymptotic (4/3)sqrt(r)(2r-d)^(3/2) yields deficit coefficient and 3/2-power negative-gap cusp; above tangency, twice differentiating exact gap area gives positive quadratic H in two regimes, continuous at r=R. Parallel-body asymptotics follow from Steiner expansion. Independent radial quadrature tested 28 (m,r/R) configurations against all exact area branches, maximum absolute error 6.73e-8; checks corroborate but do not prove the universal coverage and cusp.

originality.rationale: The key angular truncation principle resembles prior radial coverage theorems for regular POLYGON unions, but the actual objects here are congruent DISK unions with centers on a circle. Published circular-gap area laws on disk INTERSECTIONS have the opposite set operation. Finch treats a special r=R common-origin disk configuration, not the full radius threshold, optimizer family and cusp. Best knowledge leaves possible pre-existing circular disk packing and local stability results.
residual_risks: A classical or unindexed theorem might establish maximal union area for circle-constrained congruent disks; novelty of the radial inequality alone is not asserted.
The local stability expansions fix m,R,r; they do not give uniform global stability or extend to unequal radii/other center domains.
